title: Erasing the width word
statement: Let $C$ and $D$ be finite Boolean Turing machines with positive numbers of work tapes, and choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$. For any input word $w$, candidate word $s$, installed words $u,v$, and verdict bit $ok$, there is a time $t\le 2(|u|+1)$ at which the controller, started in erasure state $0$ for the left bank with these words installed, is in erasure state $2$ with verdict $ok$, the left-bank word erased, and the candidate and right-bank word unchanged; at every time $j\le t$, its state is not the anchor.
hypotheses_covered: $c_e,c_x$ are states of $C$; $d_e,d_x$ are states of $D$
replaced:
For any verdict bit, there is a time $t \le 2(\abs{u}+1)$ after which the
controller, from its first erasure seam, has blanked the installed width
word $u$ while retaining the verdict in control and preserving every other
tape; the trace avoids the anchor.
